score.moat_justification: World's largest ice cream company (~21% of the global retail ice cream market) with four power brands (Magnum, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, Heartbrand/Wall's), a proprietary freezer-cabinet estate and cold-chain scale no rival matches globally. Evidence: gross margin held 34.08% / 34.91% / 34.63% across FY2023-25 (fundamentals.json, as filed in EUR) through cocoa/dairy inflation, with +2.6% price growth AND +1.5% volume growth in FY2025 — real pricing power. The roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json reads 20.92% (FY2023) and 22.28% (FY2024), but those are carve-out years: invested capital carried almost no debt and Unilever allocated costs, so they overstate the standalone franchise; FY2025's 214.27% is a demerger artifact (equity fell to EUR 633M when EUR 2,967M of net debt was pushed onto the new balance sheet) and is not evidence. On a standalone capital base the true through-cycle ROIC is unproven — that, plus a category growing only 3-4%/yr, caps the score at 6 (moderate) rather than 7+.

analysis_md:
# MICC — The Magnum Ice Cream Company N.V.

Pass-1 run, 2026-10-19, engine release 5.4.0. In scope: market cap $11.561B at $18.78 (nasdaq_quote_api, dcf_numbers.json market_cap_est $11,560,968,000), under the $40B cutoff.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or ttm.py output — none are recomputed. Where a figure comes from the company's FY2025 results release / Form 20-F narrative (filed 2026-03-18) rather than a computed output, the source is named in line.

## What it is

The world's largest ice cream company, demerged from Unilever on 6 December 2025 and listed 8 December 2025 on Euronext Amsterdam (primary), the London Stock Exchange and the NYSE — in every market the security is the ordinary share itself (612,259,739 issued at admission; Unilever retained ~19.9%, to be sold within five years). Brands: Magnum, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto and the Heartbrand (Wall's) — ~21% of the global retail ice cream market, 30 factories, ~16,500 employees. FY2025 revenue €7,910M as filed (fundamentals.json; $9,294,250,000 after the engine's period-end FX conversion), organic sales growth +4.2% (volume +1.5%, price +2.6%). SIC 2024 — Ice Cream & Frozen Desserts.

## Owner's earnings

Engine history (financials_history.csv, USD after FX conversion at period-end ECB rates; EUR as-filed legs in fundamentals.json):

- **FY2023:** OCF $1,009,970,000 − capex $307,190,000 − SBC $22,100,000 = **OE $680,680,000**
- **FY2024:** OCF $1,156,295,700 − capex $333,486,900 − SBC $33,244,800 = **OE $789,564,000**
- **FY2025:** OCF $567,525,000 − capex $419,475,000 − SBC $41,125,000 = **OE $106,925,000**

Capex completeness (the JD/20-F trap, checked): the single filed capex tag (PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipment) is essentially the whole story — fundamentals.json shows purchases of intangibles of only €2M (FY2023) / €3M (FY2025) against PP&E capex of €278M / €321M / €357M as filed, and capex/D&A runs 0.78 / 0.85 / 1.06 across the three years — no missing-capex pattern for a manufacturer. The maintenance definition (oe_maintenance in the CSV: $649,740,000 / $675,285,000 / $331,867,000) is the same order of magnitude; the conservative OCF-based series is used throughout.

**The share-count gap and the OVERRIDE (shares).** The preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:shares` — no tier. ## Moat: 6/10 — moderate

Justification: the world's largest ice cream company (~21% global retail share) with four power brands, a proprietary freezer-cabinet estate and cold-chain scale. Evidence first: gross margin (fundamentals.json, as filed) held 34.08% / 34.91% / 34.63% across FY2023–25 through cocoa and dairy inflation, and FY2025 combined +2.6% price growth with +1.5% volume growth — proven pricing power. The roic_proxy series reads 20.92% (FY2023) and 22.28% (FY2024), but those are carve-out years on an allocated, nearly debt-free capital base and overstate the standalone franchise; FY2025's 214.27% is a demerger artifact (equity fell to €633M as the €2,967M net debt was pushed down) and is given no weight. Standalone through-cycle ROIC is unproven, and the category grows only 3–4%/yr — that caps the score at 6 rather than 7+.

- FOR: ~21% global retail share, #1 position, 30 factories — procurement and cold-chain cost advantage; power-brand portfolio (Magnum, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, Heartbrand/Wall's) with demonstrated pricing power; proprietary freezer-cabinet estate and impulse route-to-market rivals must rent or replicate; innovation cadence (150 launches in 2025; Magnum and Cornetto brands grew high-single-digit organically).
- AGAINST: category growth of only 3–4%/yr plus a structural GLP-1 appetite headwind; private label and Froneri competition; standalone economics unproven and levered (€2,967M net debt, 2.4× adjusted EBITDA); Unilever's 19.9% stake is a committed-seller overhang for up to five years; Ben & Jerry's governance conflict (independent board removed, co-founder resigned September 2025, federal litigation live); commodity (cocoa/dairy) and EM FX exposure (Türkiye hyperinflation loss €31M in FY2025).
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

No scaling is applied; per-share figures and the NYSE price are on the same basis.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE (latest FY $0.1737 vs median $1.1057):** BOTH are distorted, in opposite directions. The FY2023–24 carve-out years overstate standalone OE: they bore no allocated interest (the FY2025 release notes FY2024 finance costs "did not include any allocation of interest incurred by Unilever"), cash was swept to Unilever, and costs were allocations. FY2025 understates run-rate OE by amounts the 20-F itself itemizes. Adjusting items within operating profit were €318M in 2025 — acquisition and disposal-related costs €302M (the separation charge), restructuring €10M net, other €6M (20-F p.161) — against €200M in 2024 and €112M in 2023. The cash-flow review (p.25) itemizes €564M of Demerger-related cash outflows: €238M acquisition/disposal-related, €146M separation-related (indirect taxes paid on asset transfers, brought-forward tax payments, commodity hedge settlements) and €180M implementing the interim operating model — plus the €905M inventory subsidy paid to Unilever at Separation, held as a prepayment in trade receivables and repayable as inventory is purchased from Unilever. Set against the FY2025 OE decline of €669M vs FY2024 (€760M → €91M, EUR as filed), the demerger items are the bulk of the collapse. The interest line cuts both ways: of FY2025's €117M interest expense, €71M was interest on Unilever loans taken to fund the Separation (1 July 2025 until the Demerger, then repaid/capitalised — non-recurring) and only €16M was bond interest and fees, so FY2025 overstates one-off interest while understating a full year of bond coupons; the durable point is net finance costs of €121M in 2025 vs €17M in 2024, a carve-out year that bore no allocated Unilever interest at all. Company free cash flow printed €38M vs €803M in FY2024 on exactly these outflows. The median (FY2023 print) is used as the least-bad base; the method range is stated under Thoughts.

## My thoughts / overlay

- The honest headline is the method range, and unusually it does not change the tier: on the latest year ($0.1737/share) the weighted IRR is 3.56% (the override-impact zero-fill world); on the 6-K-bridged TTM ($0.6165/share; run recorded in dcf_numbers_ttm_bridge.json) it is 6.24%; on the pro-forma median ($1.1057/share) it is 9.14%. All three are Tier D. What the base choice changes is the hurdle price, not the verdict at $18.78 — the market is paying roughly 2× the median-base IV@15% ($9.84) for a business whose demerger year earned $0.17/share of owner's earnings.
- The bull case for the stock is a normalization story: separation costs roll off, the guided 40–60bps margin improvement lands, and OE/share recovers toward the €-carve-out prints. Even granting that in full (super bull: 1.25× base, +10.07% start) the IRR is 13.21% — still short of 15%. At $18.78 there is no scenario in the set that clears Andrew's hurdle.
- What could make this interesting later: a price near the IV@15% ($9.84), or the first clean standalone annual print (FY2026, with a full year of standalone interest and no separation costs) proving OE/share back above ~$1.30. The Unilever 19.9% sell-down (registered April 2026) is a known, dated overhang that could supply the price.
- Data quality caveats: carve-out bases, FX-at-period-end conversion, blank debt tags, and a roic_proxy series that is unusable across the demerger (20.92% / 22.28% carve-out, 214.27% artifact). This score is a screening verdict, not a precise valuation.
